% Candidate only. It is not a live-book assertion or a retirement of P06.2.
\begin{proposition}[Invariant split-toric zero-current regularity, including boundary]
\label{prop:p062-invariant-split-toric-boundary-zero-current-candidate}
Let $K$ be a complete non-Archimedean field with nontrivial valuation, let
$N$ be a lattice, let $\Sigma$ be a rational fan in $N_{\mathbb R}$, and
let $X_\Sigma$ be the associated split toric $K$-variety.  Write
\[
 \operatorname{trop}:X_\Sigma^{\An}\longrightarrow N_\Sigma
\]
for its extended tropicalization.  Let $O\subseteq N_\Sigma$ be open, put
$V=\operatorname{trop}^{-1}(O)$, and let $S$ be the maximal compact torus.
If $h:V\to\mathbb R$ is finite, continuous, and $S$-invariant, and if its
Chambert--Loir--Ducros current satisfies
\[
                         \dprimeddprime[h]=0,
\]
then $h$ is locally a smooth CLD function with zero Hessian.  In particular,
$h$ is locally $\mathbb R$-PL, harmonic in the sense of
Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff, and classically pluriharmonic.
\end{proposition}
proof:
% Dependency-closed context for independent mathematical review.
\paragraph{Target and status.}
This packet is a candidate-level P06.2 narrowing only. It does not claim an arbitrary-germ theorem, does not retire P06.2, and does not assert anything for non-invariant functions, nonsplit toric varieties, arbitrary analytic domains, or trivially valued fields.

\paragraph{Permitted primary source facts.}
The source is Burgos Gil--Gubler--Jell--K\"unnemann, \emph{Pluripotential theory for tropical toric varieties and non-Archimedean Monge--Amp\`ere equations} (BGJKK25), specifically the source extracts indexed in \texttt{SOURCE\_LEDGER.md}: invariant continuous functions on every open subset of $N_\Sigma$ descend and ascend through extended tropicalization; the proof of Proposition~5.3.10(iv) identifies their function currents by tropical pushforward; basic neighbourhoods at $N(\sigma)$ have dense part $\Omega+\sigma$ and contain the compactified normal rays; smooth tropical functions are constant towards the relevant boundary faces; and smooth tropical functions pull back to smooth CLD functions.

\paragraph{Permitted live-book interfaces.}
\Cref{prop:ch18-harmonic-basic} proves locally that a smooth function with zero CLD Hessian is a real affine combination of $-\log|f|$ for invertible analytic $f$, hence is GJR harmonic. \cite[Theorem~4.3]{GR25Classical} identifies semipositive real-PL functions on good strict analytic spaces over a nontrivially valued field with classically psh functions.

\paragraph{Audit focus.}
Check especially: (i) whether the cited pushforward computation legitimately turns $\dprimeddprime[h]=0$ into $\dprimeddprime[\varphi]=0$ for a finite continuous invariant function; (ii) the topology of the boundary basic neighbourhood and the normal-ray argument; (iii) whether the boundary slope vanishing supplies the claimed standard tropical smoothness; and (iv) whether the local harmonic and classical-pluriharmonic conclusions use no hidden boundarylessness, algebraic-closedness, or global PL hypothesis.

% Candidate only. The cited source statements and live-book interfaces are
% listed explicitly in SOURCE_LEDGER.md.
\begin{proof}
By the invariant-function correspondence (5.5) of \cite{BGJKK25}, there is
a unique finite continuous function $\varphi$ on $O$ such that
\[
                         h=\varphi\circ\operatorname{trop}.
\]
The test-form calculation in the proof of Proposition~5.3.10(iv) of
\cite{BGJKK25} applies to this continuous invariant function.  It identifies
$[\varphi]$ with $\operatorname{trop}_*[h]$, and the pushforward commutes
with $\dprimeddprime$.  The hypothesis therefore gives
\[
                         \dprimeddprime[\varphi]=0\quad\hbox{on }O.
\tag{*}\label{eq:p062-invariant-toric-boundary-zero-hessian}
\]

We show that $\varphi$ is locally smooth with zero Hessian on the tropical
toric partial compactification.  Fix $x\in O$, let $\sigma\in\Sigma$ be the
unique cone with $x\in N(\sigma)$, and choose a basic neighbourhood
$W=U(\sigma,\Omega,x_0)\Subset O$, where $\Omega\subset N_{\mathbb R}$ is
open, bounded, and convex.  As in the proof of
\cite[Theorem~3.1.4]{BGJKK25}, its dense part is
\[
                         W\cap N_{\mathbb R}=\Omega+\sigma.
\]
Restricting (*) to this open convex set shows that every distributional
second partial derivative of $\varphi$ is zero.  Thus
\[
                         \varphi(y)=\ell(y)+c
                         \qquad(y\in\Omega+\sigma)
\]
for a linear functional $\ell$ and a constant $c$.

For $y\in W\cap N_{\mathbb R}$ and $w\in\sigma$, the compactified ray
$[y,y+\infty w]$ lies in $W$.  Since $\varphi$ is finite and continuous at
its endpoint, $\ell(y+tw)+c$ has a finite limit as $t\to\infty$.  Hence
$\ell(w)=0$ for every $w\in\sigma$.  The affine function therefore descends
through $N_{\mathbb R}\to N(\sigma)$, and continuity plus density show that
it equals $\varphi$ on all of $W$.  Equivalently, $\varphi$ is constant
towards every boundary face of $W$.  Equation (3.11) of \cite{BGJKK25} then
says exactly that $\varphi$ is smooth for the standard Lagerberg structure,
and its smooth $\dprimeddprime$ is zero.

By Proposition~2.3.4 of \cite{BGJKK25}, the pullback
$h=\varphi\circ\operatorname{trop}$ is CLD-smooth on
$\operatorname{trop}^{-1}(W)$ and its smooth Hessian is zero.  The local
smooth zero-Hessian description in
\Cref{prop:ch18-harmonic-basic} writes it there as
\[
                    c+\sum_i\lambda_i\bigl(-\log|f_i|\bigr),
\]
with $f_i$ invertible.  It follows that $h$ is locally $\mathbb R$-PL and
Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff harmonic.  The analytic domain $V$ is good and
strict, and $K$ is nontrivially valued.  Applying
\cite[Theorem~4.3]{GR25Classical} to both $h$ and $-h$ makes both functions
classically psh.  Thus $h$ is classically pluriharmonic.  Since $x$ was
arbitrary, all the stated conclusions hold on $V$.
\end{proof}
